key_insight: The paper unifies neural superposition and sparse interpretable codes into one framework, showing a clear path for identifying, disentangling, and evaluating latent features in neural networks. In simple terms, it explains how multiple features can share the same representation and how to recover interpretable structure from that overlap.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of understanding and interpreting superposition in neural networks, where many latent features are packed into limited model dimensions and become difficult to separate or explain.
method: Proposes a three-step framework to identify latent features within superposed neural representations.
Provides a disentangling procedure to separate overlapping features into more interpretable codes.
Introduces evaluation criteria to assess how well the recovered features match sparse, meaningful structure.
impact: This gives AI/ML practitioners a practical conceptual toolkit for interpreting hidden representations in modern models. It can improve debugging, feature attribution, and the design of more transparent neural systems.
visual_elements: A before/after diagram showing dense superposition versus sparse interpretable codes
A 3-step pipeline graphic labeled identify → disentangle → assess
A latent-space visualization with overlapping features separated into clusters
An evaluation meter or scorecard showing interpretability and sparsity metrics
paper_title: A unifying framework from neural superposition to sparse interpretable codes
paper_authors: David Klindt, Charles O’Neill, Patrik Reizinger, Harald Maurer, Nina Miolane
